---
title: "scatterem"
subtitle: "Gap-free information transfer in 4D-STEM"
toc: false
---

A 4D-STEM dataset holds more information than any single reconstruction recovers.
Direct ptychography reads the phase gradient encoded in the bright-field disk and
recovers low and mid spatial frequencies with high efficiency, but its transfer
falls away past the disk. Tilt-corrected dark field reads the parallax shift of
scattering *outside* the disk and recovers high frequencies, but carries almost
nothing at low ones. Neither channel spans the band on its own, and used alone
each leaves a gap where the other is strong.

**Fused full-field STEM** combines them as an SSNR-weighted Wiener fusion, so each
spatial frequency is taken from whichever channel measures it better. The result
is one image with no missing band.

<a href="https://colab.research.google.com/github/scatterem/scatterem/blob/main/docs/colab/ffstem_you2026_demo.ipynb" class="colab-badge"><img src="https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg" alt="Open the demo notebook in Google Colab"></a>

Run it now on a free GPU: the notebook installs the package, fetches one dataset
from Zenodo and reconstructs it, with nothing to set up locally.

```python
from scatterem import Dataset4dstem

dataset = Dataset4dstem.from_array(
    array,                          # (scan_y, scan_x, det_y, det_x)
    energy=300e3,                   # eV
    semiconvergence_angle=19.7e-3,  # rad
    scan_step=0.25,                 # Angstrom
    device="cuda",
)

dataset.meta.aberrations.array[0] = -50.0   # starting defocus, Angstrom
dataset.determine_aberrations_(correct_order=2)

fused = dataset.fused_full_field()
```

That is the whole pipeline. Each channel is also available on its own —
`dataset.direct_ptychography()` and `dataset.tilt_corrected_dark_field()` — and
all three share one calibration, so they land on the same grid.

## Simulating core-loss STEM-EELS

The same package also runs the *forward* problem: dynamical simulation of
core-loss STEM-EELS, by conventional transition-potential multislice, by PRISM,
and by **BiP-PRISM**, which partitions both the probe-forming and the
detector-propagating scattering matrix and so fits a full-resolution elemental map
on one consumer GPU.

```python
from scatterem.simulation import StemEelsSimulator

sim = StemEelsSimulator(
    structure,                     # scatterem.simulation.Structure
    eV=100e3,
    semiconvergence_angle=25.0,    # mrad
    pixels=(128, 128),
    scan=(16, 16),
    edge=(22, 2, 1),               # Ti L: (Z, n, l)
    prism=True,
    device="cuda",
)

result = sim.simulate()            # (scan_y, scan_x, det_y, det_x)
```

See [Simulate STEM-EELS](docs/eels.qmd) for the pipeline and
[BiP-PRISM](docs/bip-prism.qmd) for the algorithm.

## Scope

Two things live here: the FF-STEM reconstruction pipeline — direct ptychography,
tilt-corrected dark field, their fusion, and the calibration and I/O they need —
and the core-loss STEM-EELS forward simulation. Each accompanies its own paper.

The wider `scatterem` codebase covers iterative ptychography and tomography;
those parts are released with their own publications.
